articles.headline: PFF ranks Michigan State's top five offensive players vs. Illinois
keyFacts: Michigan State lost their fourth consecutive game of the 2026 season against Illinois with a score of 38-37 in overtime.
Pro Football Focus ranked quarterback Alessio Milivojevic, running back Jaziun Patterson, and three other skill players as the top five offensive performers.
The Spartans aim to continue their offensive success against Northwestern in week seven.
body: Michigan State football dropped the fourth consecutive game of the 2026 season, losing a heartbreaker to Illinois, 38-37 in overtime. The margin between winning and losing fell on a two-point conversion, which the Spartans unfortunately did not convert.

A big reason the Spartans were able to overcome a 17-point deficit was due to the strong performance of the offense. Led by quarterback Alessio Milivojevic, and a strong rushing attack with Jaziun Patterson, Michigan State's offense scored a season high in points, while getting 342 yards of offense.
After looking at the film, and evaluating the game, Pro Football Focus (Subscription Required) gave out their grades for the Spartans in the game.
Check out the top five offensive players for the Spartans, according to PFF:
- QB Alessio Milivojevic - 86.9
- RB Jaziun Patterson - 78.9
- WR Bryson Williams - 73.8
- TE Jayden Savoury - 70.9
- WR Chrishon McCray - 68.0

Evidently, this is a first for the Spartans, with all five members of the top five being from skill players on the roster. A good sign of development unfolding as the Spartans aim to continue their offensive success against Northwestern in week seven.

articles.headline: 'People aren’t perfect, and everyone knows it': Security experts still see humans as the biggest threat to their business
keyFacts: A Kaseya survey found 68% of IT professionals view human error as their most concerning attack vector over the next year.
Survey findings showed that 80% of contributing factors in recent security incidents stemmed from poor user practices or lack of training.
Kaseya executive David Baggett stated that organizations must build security systems designed to withstand inevitable human mistakes.
body: - Human error remains one of the biggest challenge to online security, according to industry leaders
- 68% of security professionals cite human error, compared with just 55% for email-based scams
- A worrying 80% of contributing factors in recent security incidents can be traced back to poor user practices or lack of training
New research into the challenges facing cybersecurity professionals has revealed the naked truth: that humans are considered the main challenge to security.

A new Kaseya survey of over 1,100 MSPs and IT professionals around the world uncovered a startling trend: that the risks posed by humans to their cybersecurity are considerable. Some 68% of respondents cited human error (including social engineering and distraction) as the most concerning attack vector over the next 12 months.

With the overwhelming majority of cybersecurity incidents attributable to human error, security suites and the teams that use them are increasingly focusing on ways to mitigate the challenges posed by people.
Human error

We know that humans need security as much as the data they’re working with. But the results of this survey illustrate a sad truth: that cybersecurity professionals are more concerned about user error and the vulnerabilities of “soft” targets than the threats from automated attacks against network hardware and servers.
Hackers know that humans make mistakes. Organizations need to be on the same page.

From the results of the report, we can see that after the prospect of risks caused by human error, social engineering, and distraction, 55% of those surveyed are concerned about attacks via email. Gullibility is also considered a risk (41%) as is a lack of cybersecurity training for users (40%).
Auditing isn’t always the answer, either. Of those surveyed, 65% said they would pass a compliance audit today, but 49% noted that incomplete documentation and procedures could create problems.

True cyber resilience
Worryingly, only 20% of IT departments have a budget that is growing in line with the risks they face, with 77% describing themselves as under-resourced.
“People aren’t perfect, and everyone knows it,” noted David Baggett, SVP and GM of Security Suite at Kaseya. “Yet much of cybersecurity still depends on people making the right decision every time.”
Unfortunately, it seems as though human error is here to stay. So what is the solution? Bagget says its about factoring in the poor practices and errors.
“The path to true cyber resilience isn’t about eliminating mistakes. It’s about building an organisation that can withstand them. Expect mistakes, account for constraints and engineer around them.”
As far as Kaseya is concerned, that means building security systems and practices that withstand those mistakes.

After a postseason in which the Boston Red Sox couldn't get anything going offensively, it's safe to say the offseason will be filled with adding players on that side of the ball.
The Red Sox certainly have needs on both sides of the ball, but adding offensive help should be at the top of the priority list.

The Red Sox can do that in multiple ways, including making a trade or two. The Red Sox have farm system players they could move who should interest other teams, with the hope of getting big-time talent in return. Among the potential options, Bleacher Report recently suggested that Jeremy Pena could be one of those guys.
Pena, a World Series MVP and one-time All-Star, won't be a free agent until 2028.
“The moment Peña hired Scott Boras as his new agent in June 2025, the likelihood of a long-term extension prior to hitting the open market shrank considerably for the Astros.

“A wide-open AL West ultimately convinced the Astros to steer away from selling at the deadline, and even if they do view themselves as contenders in 2027, flipping Peña before losing him in free agency could still be on the table,” Bleacher Report wrote .
Pena is coming off a season that feels underrated, posting an impressive 124 OPS+, .802 OPS, and 22 home runs, tying for the most of his career.
As for how that fits into the Red Sox, there's no debate that adding a right-handed bat with this kind of power would immediately impact what Boston is looking to do.

articles.headline: Bumble shares soar after report dating firm in $1bn takeover talks
keyFacts: Bumble shares rose nearly 50% on Monday following reports of advanced talks to sell the company for around $1bn.
The talks come as dating apps face slowing industry growth and Bumble's valuation remains far below its 2021 peak.
The Wall Street Journal reported that technology holding company Ithaca could announce the acquisition as early as this week.
body: - Published
Shares in dating app company Bumble soared by almost 50% on Monday after a report that it is in advanced talks to be bought for around $1bn (Â£757m).
Technology holding company Ithaca could announce a deal to buy the Texas-based firm as early as this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.
The jump in Bumble's shares pushed its stock market valuation to over $580m but that is still far below a peak of more than $14bn it reached after listing on the Nasdaq in 2021.
Bumble is one of the world's most downloaded dating apps, operating in a crowded market where growth has slowed. The BBC has contacted Bumble and Ithaca for comment.
Bumble was launched in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, who was also a co-founder of dating app giant Tinder.
Wolfe Herd built Bumble's brand around a distinctive feature that only allowed women to initiate conversations with matches.
It recently abandoned that rule, prompting debate among users over whether the app had lost what set it apart from rivals.

"Today, our community is asking for more flexibility, less pressure, and more opportunities to create real, meaningful connections and that is what this new experience provides," Wolfe Herd said in August.
Dating apps like Bumble have come under pressure in recent years as some younger users have grown disillusioned with browsing for dates.
Bumble said in 2025 that it would cut almost a third of its workforce as the industry grappled with what Wolfe Herd described as an "inflection point" in online dating.
Investments in other dating companies have also soured as apps have struggled to convince users to pay for their services.
Match Group - which owns apps including Tinder, OkCupid and Hinge - has also seen its shares fall sharply from their peak in 2021.
According a report by media watchdog Ofcom in 2025, adults in the UK were spending less time on dating apps compared to three years earlier.
Some single people are instead turning to board game get-togethers, book clubs and other group activities in the hope of finding a partner.

articles.headline: Trump reveals plans for submarine repair center in Cleveland at Ohio rally
keyFacts: President Donald Trump announced that a new U.S. submarine repair center will be located in Cleveland, Ohio.
Trump made the announcement while campaigning for Ohio Republican candidates who are tied with opponents in recent polling.
Trump directed federal departments to work with senators to prevent a Youngstown utility facility from shutting down this winter.
body: President Donald Trump announced a new submarine repair center in Cleveland, Ohio , as he tries to underscore his record in the battleground state less than a month before Election Day.

“I’m … pleased to announce that the Department of War has officially selected the new home of the U.S. Submarine Component Repair Center, a big deal that everybody wanted, and it’s going to be right here in Ohio, in Cleveland, Ohio,” Trump told a crowd in Youngstown, Ohio, on Monday. “Big deal.”

Trump, who was in Ohio to support the likes of Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH) and embattled Rep. Max Miller (R-OH), in addition to Republican gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy , described how the “massive” 46,000-square-foot facility will “manufacture, repair, and maintain key parts for virtually all new and existing submarines.”
“You have to really thank Sen. Jon Husted for this more than probably anybody else,” the president said.
He added, “Look at that jawline. I’m telling you, I never saw that. I never studied him. Now I study him.”

Trump’s announcement during his second trip to Ohio in two weeks was prompted by an August presidential memorandum directing administration officials to identify a suitable location for the component repair center within 90 days.

Trump on Monday also announced that, after he was advised by Husted and Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-OH) that a steam-powered heat utility facility that provides heating for 24 major buildings in Youngstown was “in danger of shutting down as we enter the cold season,” he is directing the departments of Energy and Commerce to “work with your senators to find a quick solution and make sure it doesn’t shut down.”
“It’s going to stay open, and you’re going to stay nice and warm during the winter,” he said.

Monday’s announcements come after a flurry of similar proclamations from Trump regarding other battleground states, including a claim that South Korea has committed to spending $200 billion on U.S. energy infrastructure projects, including $50 billion on the Alaska liquefied natural gas project.
TRUMP SAYS GOP OPPONENTS OF DIESEL DEAL ‘CAN’T BE SERIOUS’

Two days after Trump made the Alaska LNG project announcement, which South Korea has disputed, the president announced that Indian-owned Mesabi Metallics will invest $15 billion to build what will be the country’s largest steel mill, with production starting in 2030.

Monday’s announcements coincide with Husted and Ramaswamy being in statistical ties with their Democratic opponents, former Sen. Sherrod Brown and Dr. Amy Acton, respectively, according to RealClearPolitics polling averages.

articles.headline: One of 2026’s Goriest Horror Movies Is Dominating HBO Max
keyFacts: Evil Dead Burn reached the No. 1 position on HBO Max's U.S. movie charts shortly after its early October streaming debut, according to FlixPatrol.
The horror film follows a grieving woman named Alice who must fight her possessed in-laws after demonic forces unleash undead monsters at a secluded family home.
Directed by Sébastien Vaniček and starring Souheila Yacoub, the movie earned a 70 percent critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes.
body: Spooky movie season is officially here, and horror fans have plenty of fresh nightmares to choose from. Obsession has been making waves, a new adaptation of Stephen King's Carrie is drawing attention, and another Resident Evil movie is bringing more video game-inspired scares to the screen.
But if you're looking for something especially gruesome to add to your October watchlist, one of this year's bloodiest horror sequels is already a streaming hit.

Evil Dead Burn arrived on HBO Max in early October and quickly climbed to the top of the service's U.S. movie charts. According to FlixPatrol, the latest entry in the long-running horror franchise reached No. 1 on HBO Max just days after its streaming debut.
What is Evil Dead Burn about?

The latest installment in the Evil Dead franchise follows Alice, played by Souheila Yacoub (Dune: Part Two), a woman grieving the death of her husband who retreats to a secluded family home with her in-laws. But the family’s attempt to process their loss quickly turns into a nightmare when demonic forces turn them into Deadites — possessed, undead monsters that attack the living — leaving Alice fighting to survive.

Directed by Sébastien Vaniček, the film also stars Tandi Wright, Hunter Doohan (Wednesday) and Luciane Buchanan (The Night Agent). It follows 2023’s Evil Dead Rise, bringing another standalone story into the franchise’s increasingly gruesome corner of horror.

The film has earned a 70% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes, suggesting that its blood-soaked approach has found plenty of admirers, even if it hasn't won over everyone. Polygon's review was less enthusiastic, arguing that Evil Dead Burn struggles to balance the franchise's two defining elements: grotesque horror and slapstick comedy. While the review praised the film's inventive kills, camera work and sound design, it found that the story's attempts to explore grief and family violence never quite come together.
But for horror fans looking to spend spooky season watching demons wreak havoc and practical effects push the limits of good taste, it could be just the sort of bloody spectacle they're after.

Saudi Arabia's energy minister has vowed a "serious" response to the deadly attacks on the kingdom's airports and oil and gas facilities by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement.
"The events of recent weeks are serious. Our response must be equally serious," Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman told the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh.

On Sunday, a Pakistani man was killed in an attack on a terminal at the capital's King Khalid International Airport, Saudi authorities said. It came a day after a Houthi missile hit another terminal, killing 13 people and forcing its closure.
The Houthis said they launched the attacks in retaliation for "brutal Saudi aggression" against areas they control in western Yemen.
The Houthi-run health ministry said a child was killed and six other people were injured in a Saudi air strike on a home in the capital, Sanaa, on Sunday.
A Saudi-led coalition is providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces battling the Houthis on Yemen's Red Sea coast and other areas.
Explosions were heard again in Riyadh on Monday night, with the Saudi-led military coalition saying a ballistic missile had been intercepted and destroyed.
A Houthi spokesperson said the group had again targeted the airport.
Meanwhile, Qatar Airways has said it will temporarily suspend flights to Riyadh and the north-eastern city of Dammam.
Etihad Airways said it had cancelled flights between Abu Dhabi and Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam due to "regional disruption".
King Khalid airport is expected to remain closed until Saturday.
The WPC Energy Congress opened on Sunday at a convention centre about 10km (6 miles) from Riyadh's airport, which has been attacked four times over the past week.
Last Thursday, three Saudis, including a pilot for the national airline Saudia, were killed in two strikes on an airport facility and an aircraft on the ground.

Another four Saudis, as well as two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian, one Sudanese and one Indian, were killed in Saturday's missile strike on Terminal 3.
On Sunday, a Pakistani resident was killed when a projectile hit Terminal 4, according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).
King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also attacked on Sunday evening, it said, but no casualties were reported.
Later, the Saudi-led coalition said its forces had intercepted a drone in Eastern Province and a missile launched by the Houthis towards the south-western city of Khamis Mushait.
In his inaugural address to the WPC Energy Congress on Monday, Prince Abdul Aziz thanked industry executives and policymakers for attending despite the attacks.
"You know this country is safe and that we hold your protection at whole heart," he said.
But he also acknowledged that "energy security cannot be taken for granted" and that recent developments had "tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience".
Prince Abdul Aziz promised that his country would overcome those challenges.
"We, as Saudis, are fearless, combatant and determined people," he said. "We shall prove it to the world that whatever we are going through we will overcome it."
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.

On Sunday evening, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said in a video statement that its forces had launched missiles and drones at Riyadh and Dammam's airports, as well as two oil and gas facilities in Eastern Province, in response to 124 Saudi air strikes in Yemen over the previous 24 hours.
Sarea also reiterated a warning to airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, except for journeys to and from the Islamic holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis' forces, he vowed, would "continue their escalating operations deep inside Saudi, imposing the equation of 'a blockade for a blockade' and 'an escalation for an escalation' and targeting Saudi enemy reinforcements until the aggression ceases and the siege on our dear people is lifted".
Saturday's attack on Riyadh airport drew widespread international condemnation.
UN Secretary General AntÃ³nio Guterres said he was "deeply shocked" and warned that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure were a violation of international law.

President Donald Trump said he would "make a decision" about the US joining Saudi Arabia's strikes on the Houthis. The US military is reportedly already providing intelligence and targeting support to the Saudi-led coalition.

Iran, which has repeatedly denied allegations that it provides weapons and training to the Houthis, said it was "deeply concerned" by the escalation and called for "dialogue and engagement" to resolve the situation.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The Yemeni government claimed it was behind that strike, saying it was trying to prevent an unauthorised Iranian plane from landing.

Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the southern end of the Red Sea.
They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure of the strait contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports after the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in the Gulf.
Last week, the Yemeni government announced the start of a new offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis.
Pro-government forces said they were quickly able to retake areas around Bab al-Mandab with the help of intense Saudi air strikes, but the Houthis denied losing any territory.

articles.headline: Brewers two wins from first World Series since 1982 as Contreras skewers Dodgers
keyFacts: William Contreras drove in the tying and go-ahead runs as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 7-4 on Monday.
The victory gave the Brewers a 2-0 lead in the National League Championship Series, putting them two wins away from the World Series.
The series shifts to Los Angeles for Game 3 on Wednesday as the Dodgers attempt to overcome the 2-0 deficit.
body: William Contreras hit a tying homer in the fifth and singled home the go-ahead run an inning later as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 7-4 on Monday in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series.

Four relievers combined to retire the last 15 Dodgers batters in order as the Brewers took a 2-0 lead over the two-time defending World Series champions in this best-of-seven series, which heads to Los Angeles for Game 3 on Wednesday.

The Brewers are chasing their second pennant and first in the NL. They made their lone World Series appearance in 1982, when they were in the American League. Los Angeles are trying to become the first NL team to win three straight World Series.

The Dodgers last rallied from a 2-0 deficit to win a series in 2020, when they beat the Atlanta Braves in a seven-game NLCS before going on to win the World Series. The Dodgers will need more punch from their lineup to have a chance at getting back to the Fall Classic. They mustered just three hits on Monday and went 0 for 4 with runners in scoring position to drop to 2 for 26 in those situations this postseason.
Los Angeles couldn’t even get a boost from Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who entered 8-1 with a 2.14 ERA in 11 career playoff appearances. Yamamoto lasted just 2.2 innings for his shortest postseason start.

The Dodgers took the lead on three occasions in the first five innings. Milwaukee responded each time, the last coming when Contreras tied the game with a 436ft homer to center off Kris Bubic in the fifth.

That turned the game into a battle of the bullpens, where the Brewers again had the edge. Dustin May, JoJo Romero, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined to shut down the Dodgers after Logan Henderson’s early exit.

The score was tied 4-4 when Milwaukee’s David Hamilton was hit by a pitch from Brock Stewart to lead off the sixth. Stewart attempted a pickoff throw that went off the glove of first baseman Freddie Freeman and into foul territory for an error, advancing Hamilton to second.
After Jackson Chourio grounded out, the right-handed Stewart walked the left-handed-hitting Brice Turang to face the right-handed Contreras, who had homered in his previous plate appearance.
Contreras singled to left this time to bring home Hamilton with the go-ahead run.
Turang and Jake Bauers added RBI singles in the eighth to extend Milwaukee’s lead.

articles.headline: 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte dies
keyFacts: American actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte died on Monday at age 34, his management agency stated.
Mitte was recognized for his breakout role as Walter White Jr. in the drama series Breaking Bad.
Mitte had cerebral palsy and served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Hospitals for Children.
body: American actor RJ Mitte, whose lived experience with cerebral palsy was channeled into a key role in "Breaking Bad," died on Monday at the age of 34.
"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," his management agency said in a statement.
No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.

In addition to his breakout role in in "Breaking Bad" and later credits including "Switched at Birth" and "Guardians of Justice," Mitte also served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Hospitals for Children.
An 'authentic' breakout role

In "Breaking Bad," Mitte played Walter White Jr., the son of Bryan Cranston's character, chemistry teacher-turned-meth dealer Walter White. Mitte's character used crutches and spoke with a slur, and gained greater prominence as the series progressed.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement said.
"Breaking Bad" ran from 2008 until 2023. With 16 Emmy awards, it's often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time.

Shortly after the series wrapped up, Mitte told the Associated Press that his disability and the surrounding struggles with physical therapy, family problems and exorbitant medical bills — all of which featured in the show — made him better in his role.
"You develop a different mentality and you develop a different look at how the world sees you and how you see the world," he said in 2024.
"You're able to use that. And I think it's an asset instead of something that would hinder," Mitte added.

articles.headline: Hurricane Simon lashes Mexico's Pacific coast, pounds resorts and towns
keyFacts: Hurricane Simon weakened to a Category 2 storm while pounding west-central Mexico's coast with damaging winds and rain, forecasters said.
Mexican officials evacuated at-risk residents and urged sheltering across multiple states due to predicted life-threatening flooding and mudslides.
Forecasters expect Simon to approach Mexico's coast midweek and bring heavy rain to the U.S. Southern Plains through Friday.
body: Hurricane Simon weakened Monday to a Category 2 storm, but it continued to pound the coast of west-central Mexico as its eye remained just offshore.

Dangerous winds lashed the region, threatening coastal areas with flooding rain, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said. With its center still swirling near the coast, Simon's most damaging winds and rain were forecast to persist near the Puerto Vallarta area, a coastal town known for its beach resorts.

The storm's maximum sustained winds have decreased below the 111 mph storm, as it was previously categorized, according to the hurricane center. Simon had been weakening gradually since the early hours of Monday morning, but forecasters warned it could strengthen again, and, regardless, it remained a dangerous hurricane.
Map shows hurricane's path
On Monday night, Simon's eye was about 80 miles west of Cabo Corrientes and inching west-northwestward at about 3 mph, the hurricane center said.

The storm was expected to change directions midweek and eventually approach the coast of west-central Mexico on Wednesday into Thursday. The hurricane center warned that Simon "could re-intensify some" and "is expected to remain a hurricane through midweek" before it weakens and moves inland.

Simon is expected to bring heavy rain to the U.S. Southern Plains from Tuesday afternoon through Friday morning, CBS News and Stations meteorologist Nikki Nolan said. That region could see 3 to 5 inches of rain and more in some places.

Hurricane-force winds were extending outward up to 10 miles, and tropical storm-force winds were reaching up to 45 miles from Simon's center, meaning the entire area between Mexico's western coast and the Sierra Madre mountains could be affected.
Hurricane warnings and watches for Simon

A hurricane warning is in effect for Las Islas Marias, which means hurricane conditions are expected in the area. A hurricane watch is in effect along the coast of Mexico from Cabo Corrientes to Bahia Tempehuaya, where hurricane conditions are possible within the next two days.

A senior hurricane center specialist, Philippe Papin, said the westernmost tip of mainland Mexico is the area most likely to get a direct hit from the system. Cabo Corrientes is at the southern tip of Bahia de Banderas, the wide bay where Puerto Vallarta looks out to the Pacific.

"We're expecting catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts along that west-central coast of Mexico where the hurricane warning is currently in effect," Papin said. "They're also getting very heavy rainfall associated with the storm that's likely going to produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides in areas of higher terrain along the Mexican coastline, and there will be significant swells."

The hurricane center said early Monday that Simon was expected to dump an additional 2 to 4 inches of rain, with some areas getting up to 8 inches, in the states of Colima, Jalisco, Nayarit and Sinaloa through early Thursday.

"Isolated maximum storm totals of 30 inches are possible over portions of the states of Michoacan, Colima, and Jalisco," the center said in its latest advisory. "This rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides or worsen any ongoing flooding, especially in areas of steep terrain."
Tourists arrive as Puerto Vallarta residents brace for Simon

Puerto Vallarta is a popular tourist destination in the state of Jalisco. Just inland and uphill from the resort areas, many Mexicans live in communities where housing might not stand up to the storm.

As the storm approached Puerto Vallarta, National Guard vehicles patrolled the streets while police used a megaphone to call out the few people who were jogging, walking their dogs or biking by the waterfront. Officers reminded people that the area was closed and urged them to take shelter. Not everyone followed the orders.

Jalisco state suspended classes on Friday and Monday in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating people from at-risk areas while asking the tourism sector to make sure workers and visitors are fully accommodated in shelters or safe zones.

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum took to social media to urge people in Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacan to stay sheltered until the government issues a notification that the danger has passed. She also asked people to follow recommendations from civil protection officials and to avoid traveling on public roads.
"Precautionary evacuation efforts to safe zones are ongoing; the priority is our safety," she wrote.

Hotel worker Víctor Martínez went shopping for nonperishable food Sunday afternoon. He said he couldn't go to work because public transportation service was suspended and most of the hotel had been evacuated.
Martínez found people's concerns about the hurricane comforting.

"It happened to us before. It hit us years ago," Martínez said, referring to a Category 5 hurricane that hit the area in 2002. "People didn't expect it. We were very skeptical that it would ever hit us. Now, though, we're different. Precautions are being taken. It happened to us once, and we won't let it happen again."
Despite the risks posed by Simon, tourists were still arriving in Puerto Vallarta.

Visitors Ricardo Ramírez and Brenda Villarreal, who have never lived through a hurricane, went looking for food by the city's boardwalk and came across police urging people to take shelter. Ramírez said they were completely unprepared for the situation.
"The boardwalk is closed. Be responsible. Understand!" police told passersby using a megaphone.
Ramírez said he and Villarreal had planned their four-day vacation since last year and traveled from Guadalajara, Jalisco's capital.
"We don't know the extent of the danger yet," Villarreal said. "We're just starting to see what's going on."

Unlike the Atlantic, which saw just of the season this week with Isaias, the Pacific season has been very active. Simon's arrival comes on the heels , which slammed Mexico as a Category 2 hurricane before reaching the southwestern U.S. and bringing heavy flooding to the region.

articles.headline: One dead and several injured after roller coaster incident at Six Flags Over Georgia
keyFacts: A man died and at least four others were injured after an incident on a roller coaster, according to news reports.
Six Flags Over Georgia closed immediately, and a spokesperson stated the park is cooperating fully with local authorities.
The Cobb County Police Department said its major crimes unit is investigating the death.
body: A man died on Monday after apparently falling out of a roller coaster at a Six Flags location in Georgia , according to news reports.

The circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. At least four other people were injured. Officials evacuated riders from the roller coaster at the amusement park, video footage posted on social media shows.

“We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today,” a spokesperson for Six Flags Over Georgia said. “Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest’s family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected.”

“The park team and local authorities responded immediately, and we are cooperating fully with local authorities as they complete their investigation,” the spokesperson added. “Out of respect for the family’s privacy, we will not be sharing additional details at this time.”
The Cobb County Police Department said its major crimes unit is investigating the incident. The Washington Examiner contacted the police department for further comment.

The death came about two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain in Los Angeles County, California , announced it would retire its X2 roller coaster following a CNN investigation that exposed more than a dozen reports of injuries and deaths in connection with the ride.

The 200-foot-tall roller coaster, known as “Goliath,” was halted during the emergency. The man who died reportedly hit the track multiple times as he fell to the ground. The park was immediately shut down following his death.

articles.headline: Don't buy a cheap Android phone without these non-negotiable features
keyFacts: Engadget reported buyers should prioritize at least 6GB of RAM, 128GB of storage, and capable processors when selecting budget Android phones.
The guide stated recommended devices also need minimum 5.6-inch AMOLED screens, 4,500mAh batteries, and 32-megapixel rear cameras for basic functionality.
Shoppers can find qualifying devices from Samsung, Motorola, Nothing, or Google by waiting for seasonal promotions, according to Engadget.
body: Don't buy a cheap Android phone without these non-negotiable features
What good is a phone that can't keep up with the average person's day-to-day needs?

You don't have to spend an arm and a leg on an Android phone, even if it's brand-new. You can find plenty of great cheap Android phone options for $300 or less, if you know what to look for. And that's the biggest thing to consider: knowing what features are crucial to have and where you can make concessions. Paying less for a phone that doesn't have a sleek titanium frame, for example, is totally fine; you probably will (and should) put a case on it, anyway. But getting a phone with insufficient RAM, horrible battery life, poor cameras, a bad processor, or a small screen is where you want to draw the line.

In some cases, what you're willing to sacrifice is an individual decision. If you're a casual content creator, for example, the cameras need to be at least above average. But if you're getting a secondary phone for basic messaging, you may be fine with just decent cameras. Nonetheless, there are some non-negotiable limits that anyone seeking out a cheap Android phone should focus on, no matter how you plan to use it.
Screen and RAM minimums

Remember when phones had tiny screens? The original iPhone's 4.5-inch screen seemed groundbreaking at the time, but by today's standards, that just doesn't cut it. A phone should have at least a 5.6-inch screen, though most nowadays are at least 6.1 inches. This allows you to enjoy a comfortable experience when holding the phone and typing two-handed while still being able to clearly see the content on it. That screen should also be an AMOLED panel with HD resolution and a decent peak brightness of at least 1,000 nits, so it's viewable in direct sunlight.

Memory is another factor to consider. You'll want at least 6GB RAM; otherwise, multitasking, video streaming, and casual gaming could be slow or inconsistent, and the phone won't respond quickly enough to your demands. If you play a lot of mobile games, consider even going up to 8GB. Also, if there's no expandable storage (which is a rarity nowadays), 128GB is the minimum you should consider. For peace-of-mind, go with at least 256GB. Otherwise, you'll end up with a "phone full" message before you know it, and you'll be forced to clear out the device or sign up for cloud storage.

Finally, the processor matters. While you might not need the best, fastest, most up-to-date processor, you don't want one that's slow as molasses. Check the age of the processor, as well as reviews for its performance, and factor this into your decision. There's no value in getting a cheap device if it's slow and laggy when you want to stream a movie, and a great processor is vital for gaming on an Android phone.
Don't skimp on the battery and cameras

Battery life and cameras are also important. A battery that's at least 4,500mAh is sufficient, especially if the phone doesn't handle heavy AI processing. But 5,000mAh is a better starting point nowadays to keep you going all day, even with moderate use. With cameras, you want a phone that can at least take photos that are good enough for sharing on social media and keeping for posterity. This means having at least a 32MP sensor for the rear camera, but also a large sensor that can capture more light and yield better photos overall, even if the megapixels are lower in one camera versus another. Don't discount the front sensor and resolution as well, as this is what you'll use to take selfies. Look for at least a 12MP front camera with, again, a good sensor size.

Consider other basics like NFC for tap-to-pay and more recent Bluetooth versions for reliable connectivity to headphones and speakers. For older models, confirm that there's at least a few years left of software and security support. This sounds like a lot, but you'll find plenty of devices that fit, like Samsung's Galaxy A series phones (see our review of the Samsung Galaxy A17, for example) and phones from brands like Nothing and Motorola.

Even older-model Google Pixel phones can fit the criteria. You can find a renewed Google Pixel 8a for just over $300 nowadays, and it comes with just about every vital feature mentioned previously. Ideally, wait for seasonal promotions to find a decked-out mid-range phone for the price of a budget one. You'll have to make compromises to go cheap, but there are many phones in the $300 range that meet or exceed non-negotiable features and specs.

articles.headline: Want Your New iPhone Duo Fast? Lock in Your Details Now
keyFacts: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, during an event led by new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus.
The device features a 7.6-inch folding display and ranges from $1,999 to $3,199, making it Apple's most expensive iPhone.
Shoppers can save their purchase details on Apple's staging page before official preorders open at 5 a.m. PT on Friday.
body: If you’re eager to get your hands on the highly anticipated iPhone Duo, the first foldable iPhone, here’s how to get a head start on ordering. Apple has opened a staging page for preorders on apple.com, where you can get ready to place a preorder for the viral phone.

Head over to Apple’s online storefront, and you’ll find that a new iPhone Duo configurator is now live. On that page, save your preferred phone color, storage, mobile carrier and payment method. Saving these details in advance ensures you can complete your purchase immediately when preorders open at 5 a.m. PT on Friday.

Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, one of its first new products under the helm of new CEO John Ternus, during its Surprise and Shine event in Cupertino, California, on Friday. It’s the first foldable from Apple, although merely the latest in a wave of new bendy phones to hit the market.

The iPhone Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch display and folds down to a pocketable passport size. The shifting shape supports split-screen multitasking and Apple Pencil, and brings a host of new features and animations to Apple iOS 27.

Pricing starts at $1,999 for the 512GB model and tops out at $3,199 for the 2TB version — before carrier subsidies — making the iPhone Duo the most expensive iPhone ever released. Price aside, observers expect demand among early adopters to be high, so prepping your order now is a smart idea.

Not quite sure that the new iPhone Duo is the right phone for you? I’m also on the fence. Check out CNET’s coverage leading up to the launch of the new foldable and iOS 27, as well as the more conventionally shaped iPhone 18 Pro, so you can make an informed decision.

articles.headline: Jaissle sorry for Coventry loss as Carra says Newcastle 'beaten up' again
keyFacts: Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle apologised to fans after his team suffered a 4-1 away defeat against Coventry.
Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher stated that Newcastle had been beaten up physically in their last two away matches.
The 4-1 loss follows a previous 4-1 away defeat at Leeds, leaving Newcastle in 11th place in the Premier League table.
body: Matthias Jaissle: Newcastle boss apologises for Coventry loss as Jamie Carragher says they were 'beaten up'

Newcastle suffer second consecutive 4-1 away loss after defeat at Coventry; Toon boss Matthias Jaissle: "We can only apologise to the fans who came here"; Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher: "In their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly"
Monday 12 October 2026 23:46, UK
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has apologised to the travelling fans following their 4-1 loss at Coventry, as Jamie Carragher said they were "beaten up" once again on the road.
The Magpies' previous away game a month ago also saw them defeated 4-1 on the Monday Night Football at Leeds.
A second loss in three games comes after Jaissle had enjoyed an unbeaten five-game start across all competitions, but recent results have seen his side fall to 11th in the Premier League table.
A wasteful Newcastle lost at Coventry despite having 19 shots, three big chances and more than double the number of touches in the opposition box than the home side.

Jaissle told Sky Sports: "We're frustrated. It's a feeling you don't want to have on a Monday evening after a match where you should win.
"We can only apologise to the fans who came here; they deserve a different result.
"We need to analyse it, clearly. There were bits that were good but, in both boxes, to defend our own goal we need to improve and also score goals.
"The opportunities were there, but the desire and hunger to finish the attacks was missing."
He added: "We need to improve on the things we can control, and that's a lot right now."
Newcastle have now conceded the joint-most goals in the league so far alongside Bournemouth and Chelsea.
The German said at his post-match press conference: "I think it was a tough story throughout the whole match. There were elements in both boxes where we need to step up and improve.
"It's not something we can compare with the Leeds match today because I think we were at least better.
"The goals we conceded, it was a different story. We were better after the first 10 minutes; we dominated the game but conceded easy goals, which we need to improve.
"If you conceded eight goals in two away matches on Monday evenings, then it's not good enough for the Premier League."
Carra: Newcastle 'beaten up' again
It is the first time since December 2012 that Newcastle have conceded four or more goals in back-to-back Premier League away games.
For Carragher, the heavy losses at Leeds and Coventry have raised questions over Newcastle's "lack of physicality".
Speaking on Monday Night Football, Sky Sports' Carragher said: "We've consistently said this season they've had a good start results-wise, but the underlying numbers haven't been great.
"How many shots they concede, their xG. You look at two away games now where they've lost 8-2.
"He's going with two strikers up there; I know (Yoane) Wissa drops a little bit deeper, but when Eddie Howe was there it was more of a 4-3-3.
"Every manager has their own way, but when you think of the lack of physicality in that team, it might be a case where you leave one of the strikers out and go with an extra body in midfield.
"It's a young team, and it isn't as physically powerful as a lot of the teams in the Premier League.
"And in their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly."
Analysis: Coventry teach Newcastle a lesson in finishing
Sky Sports' Ron Walker:
On a night where they faced the Premier League's second-highest xG overperformers, it was Coventry who taught Newcastle a lesson in finishing at the CBS Arena.
It was one they had learned the hard way too, with the worst shot conversion of any team in the league coming into Monday's game and just one of 51 shots finding the back of the net to date.
But football is a funny old game. A 4-1 scoreline suggests Newcastle were outplayed, which could not be further from the truth, though they were certainly outfought.

Where Coventry stood resilient - even clearing off their own line from Matias Fernandez-Pardo once he had rounded Carl Rushworth - Newcastle caused too many of their own problems, and, for once, the Sky Blues took full advantage.

Three superb finishes, and an early penalty, saw them to their first Premier League home win in more than 9,000 days, but their finishing was still not Coventry's most impressive quality on the night.

That fortitude, digging in after taking an early lead and hanging on after Sven Botman's wonder strike had given Newcastle a glimmer of hope at 2-1, was what won them the day and, on fight at least, that was enough to crown them worthy winners.

They have already needed that mental strength to bounce back from four goalless and pointless games to start their Premier League return, and, in a league as punishing as this, that could be what decides whether they will stay there come May.

articles.headline: VR Chat Community Protests An Influx Of AI Slop Onto Platform, Hurting Discoverability
keyFacts: A prominent VR Chat volunteer stopped their community work in protest of an influx of generative AI content hurting search discoverability.
Developers responded by immediately banning deceptive AI thumbnails and launching a community consultation to shape future AI policies.
Consultations will continue for one week, after which the developers promise to share their findings and enact new AI policies.
body: The VR Chat community has entered an uproar surrounding the use of Generative AI on the platform, following a volunteer community memberâs announcement they will halt their activities in protest at the increasing influx of the technology in popular worlds. With debates on its impact to discovering new communities and the varied opinions on AI within the community on the app, the developers have launched a community policy regarding where to draw the line on generative AI usage in creative and player-facing spaces moving forwards.

With this also impacting discoverability and varied opinions on the technology, it has led the developers to issue a community consultation on creating a policy for the use of generative AI tools in the creation and player activities of the application moving forwards.

For its users, VR Chat has become the metaverse Mark Zuckerberg wished he could create: the free app is a hub for fan-created worlds and maps where groups of people can freely meet, talk and interact with one another, as well as conduct and share their own art or engage in dedicated niche communities. Itâs even been adopted by some companies, with the tool being used as the basis for official virtual events and concerts. In-app purchases and subscriptions alongside merchandising keep the service running, with players themselves building an ecosystem for commissions on avatar costumes and free tools to support other users.

Of these community developers, Patroll is one of the most prominent, working on the applicationâs fan-run wiki and aiding with community testing and translation. Due to the ârampant plagueâ of AI-generated worlds and images, including the creation of AI-generated thumbnail previews for worlds in search that deceptively represent their content, they have chosen to step back from their community work, and requested other developers to include banners explicitly stating no AI is used in their work until more is done to aid in filtering out AI, minimize the use of AI internally at the developers VR Chat, amongst other demands.

AI's a rampant plague that @VRChat refuses to address. VRC promotes AI worlds & uses AI images. Until something changes, I'm stopping my efforts in VRChat translations, VRChat Wiki maintenance and Community Testers, as well as spending money on the platform. Join group NOAI.3843. pic.twitter.com/sTMssCor7j
— Patroll (@P4tr0ll) October 4, 2026

Many users joined this protesters, leading to many of the most popular worlds to display the banner prominently within the app. The strong community response has led the company to respond directly in their own statement, detailing what they view as acceptable usecases of AI while seeking to consult other users on how to address its broader use cases. Alongside immediately banning deceptive thumbnails, the company admits it finds itself at an âuncomfortable crossroadsâ.

âOn one hand, AI can help accelerate development and ease technical burden, while on the other, it can generate endless streams of low-quality, low-effort content that erodes human connection,â they note in a statement.

Beyond thumbnails, their immediate policy shift condones the use of AI for translation, code help (using Copilot to write code), so-called AI-powered tools within development engines like Blender or Unity, as well as building tools for personal use. User-facing uses of AI, such as building physics of game logic for a world, using AI assets or fully generating a world, they feel there is âuncertaintyâ on how far to allow the use, asking users to share their views on whether to label or even fully-prohibit these use-cases. The company also promises to improve search to prioritize higher-quality discovery, in the hope it removes âslopâ from searches. Full labeling of worlds, due to the risk of mislabeling and policing, remains an unconfirmed option.

The response has been mixed. While some see it as a step in the right direction, others question why the labeling as a filter is even a debate and not something the company immediately enact for those who want it. Patroll, the leader of this protest, has asked the team to go further, hoping for ways for players to build their own discovery systems.

For a service powered by its community and users such as this, as the debates surrounding AI become more intense amongst both the technologyâs supporters and detractors, can there be common ground when some feel it is stealing their work and others believe in the technology? Consultations will continue for the next week, after which the team promise to share their findings and enact their AI policies moving forwards.

articles.headline: 'Our humble goal is to survive the AI revolution' says Epic Games CEO, as its Star Wars and Marvel crossover pivots to 'AI first' development
keyFacts: Epic Games has delayed an unannounced Star Wars and Marvel shooter indefinitely and instructed its creators to adopt an AI-first development approach.
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said the company is moving developers to retool for maximum AI acceleration using tools like Anthropic's Claude.
Sweeney stated that the company's goal is to survive the AI revolution and help other developers make better code and content faster.
body: An unannounced Star Wars and Marvel shooter in the works at Epic Games has been delayed, and its creators instructed to take an "AI first" approach to development. Staff were advised of the pivot last week, according to a Bloomberg report, with the project delayed indefinitely from its (unannounced) March 2027 release.

That "AI first" approach seems pretty comprehensive: the instructions per Bloomberg are to "implement an 'AI first' production model using tools such as Anthropic's Claude". Art will be "generated with full AI workflows", according to the same set of instructions.
Shortly after Bloomberg's report was published, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney took to X to share his own thoughts:

- On AI use at Epic Games in general: "We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration," he said. "The aim isn't to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal."

- On Epic 'not reading the room' when it comes to consumer attitudes towards generative AI: "Much of the room wants it to be 2016 again, but it's not. Our job, as the provider of tools and technology to much of the industry, is to design for the present that is and the future that will soon be. Personally I'm optimistic about it and see it as empowering for creators."

- On whether Epic will "accelerate an IPO": "Our more modest aim is to survive the AI revolution, help other developers do the same, and come out on the other end making better code and content faster."

- On potential improvements to development time offered by AI: "Right now it's highly variable, from 20% in some areas (like the most technical areas of UE [Unreal Engine] dev) to 5x for other areas (like web dev). By this time next year I expect very little will be less than 3x of January 2026 efficiency."

- On AI's effects on game design in general: "The biggest change will be much faster time from having an idea to playtesting it. This will be great for gameplay, as most of the recent AAA failures can be attributed to game systems going through far too much of their development process without being able to playtest.

Epic Games laid off over 1,000 employees in March, citing the decline in console sales, Epic's ongoing legal disputes with Apple and Google, and difficulty in delivering "consistent Fortnite magic with every season".
Are projects like Epic Games' Star Wars x Marvel crossover inevitable? Will we just have to cope?

Let's be honest: a Marvel and Star Wars crossover shooter made by Epic Games, predominantly utilising generative AI and AI workflows, will be a pretty fascinating experiment to behold. It's such a rich intersection of exhaustingly ubiquitous pop culture touchstones that there's every possibility its AI origins will be less detectable than they might otherwise be.

Because AI slop already mostly looks like Fortnite, Star Wars and Marvel. Add Pixar (which Fortnite looks like), and you basically have slop Mount Rushmore. This is the abyss staring back into the abyss.

Sweeney's quote about audiences wishing they were still in 2016 is telling. The AI industry loves to frame uptake of the technology as an inevitability that detractors / luddites will just need to cope with, or at least, they do when they're not loudly worrying that the technology might kill us.
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

Still, terrible things that no one likes do have a way of bleeding inescapably into our everyday lives. Tech companies own platforms best equipped to make us tolerate things we innately abhor. People hated Facebook's rollout of "likes"—now most of us "like" things with our mouths firmly closed. People hated it when social media feeds stopped being feeds, so that, for example, weird videos about putting various objects through meat grinders are now mainstream. The transformation from "way to catch up with friends" into "ruinously addictive habit" wasn't appreciated, but it's the norm now anyway.
In other words, the tech industry knows that it doesn't matter whether you like it or not: you'll get what you're given.

articles.headline: Duelist: Idle Expedition class tier list
keyFacts: Destructoid published a class tier list for the game Duelist: Idle Expedition, dividing seven base classes into S, A, and B tiers.
The Warrior and Mage are ranked in the S-tier, while the Priest, Thief, and Orc are placed in the A-tier.
The Archer is placed in the B-tier, and the Elf was omitted from the list pending further assessment.
body: Duelist: Idle Expedition has seven different base classes to pick from, and all of them have different pros and cons. Ideally, you can do well with any class you want as long as the build is on point.
In this guide, I will assess all seven available classes for you to pick from.
Table of contents
Complete Duelist: Idle Expedition class tier list S-tier
A-tier
B-tier
Complete Duelist: Idle Expedition class tier list
To separate all seven classes, I have used three different tiers.
S-tier classes are pretty much the best possible choices.
A-tier classes are close to S-tier, but you’ll need to get your build on point.
B-tier classes are really difficult to manage, and you’ll want to min-max your build.
S-tier

Warrior: This is the most beginner-friendly choice. It offers good damage, decent survivability, and a lot of versatility in terms of how its subclasses work. This is also an excellent choice to learn the game, so that’s another big positive. With the correct build, you can use the Warrior to reach the endgame easily.

Mage: the Mage is one of the best options when it comes to ranged damage. While the damage potential is very high, the mage can also inflict plenty of elemental affixes on the enemy. This makes the class a good choice for different combinations and runs.
A-tier

Priest: The Priest is really useful when it comes to healing, and there is no other class that does it better. In some ways, this makes the Priest a must-use in almost any combination, but the base damage would have been slightly higher to help clear the harder bosses.

Thief: The Thief has immense damage potential among all melee classes, but you will have to be extremely specific with its build. Unlike the Warrior or the Orc, the Thief does not have a lot of health to begin with, so getting a proper setup with a complementary squad is necessary.

Orc: The Orc is a pretty decent choice for most players, as it deals an immense amount of physical damage. That said, when I compare it to the Warrior, the Orc requires a bit more love in terms of the equipment you are using.
B-tier

Archer: With the correct setup, the Archer can be one of the best ranged attackers to add to any squad. The class also works well with almost all other classes equally, but it needs a lot of care. Go for the wrong build, and you will end up with suboptimal results. This is why I have put the class in the BTO.

The only class I have not placed on the tier list is the Elf. I would like to assess it more over time and with some proper builds. The remaining classes I have ranked above will give a good idea of how to run an optimal squad.

articles.headline: Coventry announce themselves back in the big time
keyFacts: Coventry defeated Newcastle with four goals to end their 25-year wait for a home win and goal in the Premier League.
Manager Frank Lampard stated that the victory lifted the team out of the relegation zone and provided good confidence.
Teenager Sidiki Cherif scored his first goal for Coventry and became the club's youngest Premier League goalscorer since 2000.
body: - Published
The last time Coventry won at home in the Premier League former Spice Girl Emma Bunton was top of the charts with 'What Took You So Long?'
The title could not be more fitting as the Sky Blues ended their 25-year wait for a top-flight goal and victory in front of their own fans.
Baby Spice's song may not live long in the memory but Coventry's thumping win over Newcastle will stick with the home supporters.
Jack Rudoni's penalty, Sidiki Cherif's first Sky Blues goal and late strikes from Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni lifted them out of the relegation zone in style.
Level on points with Manchester United after six games and out of the drop zone following successive wins, Frank Lampard's men have announced themselves in the top flight again.
Coventry backed up their victory at Nottingham Forest before the international break, scoring four goals in the top flight for the first time since a 4-1 win over Sheffield Wednesday in May 2000.
Those around the Sky Blues' training ground at Ryton feel that, if they are competitive over the next seven games, they will have a platform for survival.
A trip to Tottenham and the visit of Fulham - both winless - come next, with games against Sunderland, Everton, Crystal Palace, Leeds and Ipswich to take them into December.
"It's big and we have to tap into that in a good way, in a humble way," said Lampard, whose side are now 14th.
"We have to be excited and I'm seeing players in my eyes that are developing quite quickly.
"A lot of players had low Premier League minutes, or zero Premier League minutes - Jack Rudoni, [Brandon] Thomas Asante, [Ephron] Mason-Clark, a lot of them.
"So is it human nature in the first few games we've had two top teams in the league (Arsenal and Manchester City) and we've had Brighton and we've gone: 'hmm, it's not easy here'.
"This [win] gives good confidence, so it's the balance of confidence against overconfidence. But it's great when you have a template of feeling when you get a result of that level."
It can be a defining six weeks for Lampard's men after a resounding, if not perfect, win against Newcastle.
Coventry's previous home games had seen them fall to a 1-0 defeat by fellow promoted side Hull before a 5-0 thumping by Brighton.
Sandwiched in the middle was a 3-1 loss to Aston Villa in the Carabao Cup, meaning it was imperative they found form at the CBS Arena.
"We're going to be a relative underdog in pretty much every game," added Lampard. "So we have to maximise everything and be on the limit and I thought we were on the limit in loads of ways.
"They need to keep their feet on the ground because the next one's tough and the one after that will be tough.
"But we look like a team that [will make it] hard for teams to come here. That's the feeling we haven't quite had in our first CBS games this season."
Cherif of Coventry makes his mark
Lampard handed a first Premier League start to Cherif after his summer move from Fenerbahce and the teenager repaid the faith.
"We've got a lot of belief in Sidi, a big signing for the club," said Lampard, after inflicting a second successive 4-1 away defeat for the Magpies.

"He's very respectful but there's a hunger that flicks on when he goes on to the training pitch and in game. I felt it from our first meeting and I've seen it in training, he wants to train and do well.

"Sometimes you don't realise he's 19. He'll be disappointed with the one he missed and I've said to him it's no problem because that's good. You get there, you get hungry, you go again. He's got that little edge to him in a good way."
At 19 years and 301 days old, Cherif is Coventry's youngest Premier League goalscorer since Robbie Keane against Middlesbrough in April 2000 (19y 282d).
He is also the first player to score a Premier League goal from outside the box for the Sky Blues since David Thompson struck against Newcastle in January 2001.
His crisp finish, though a forest of defenders, was a first in his fourth appearance for Coventry, having already won the early penalty.
Coventry scored 97 goals as they won the Championship last season and the ruthless nature of their finishing was a reminder of their striking power.
With Hadji Wright still out with a serious thigh injury, much of the goalscoring burden will fall on Â£20m Cherif, who was not even born the last time Coventry were in the Premier League.
Lampard said: "Sidi has played in European competition with Fenerbahce, so there is something about him that hopefully feels like he belongs on the level.
"There's something about him I think is a bit special."

articles.headline: "No more hand-written code": Epic reportedly impose "AI-first" model on creators of new Disney shooter with Marvel and Star Wars characters
keyFacts: Epic Games has reportedly instructed developers of an unannounced Disney shooter to adopt an AI-first production model using tools like Claude.
According to a Bloomberg report, the game's director allegedly stated there would be no more hand-written code and all art would be AI-generated.
Epic communications director Jake Jones stated the company is embracing AI-accelerated development led by human developers, while Disney has not commented.
body: The happy-go-lucky bigwigs at Epic Games have instructed the creators of an unannounced shooter that features Marvel and Star Wars characters to complete their project using an "AI first" production model, according to a report, with generated art and code. The Disney collaboration in question was allegedly due for release in March, but has now been delayed indefinitely. The game's makers are, we're told, being ordered to make heavier use of Anthropic's Claude and similar tools.

The report in question is from Bloomberg, who cite "people familiar with the project", together with an alleged internal message from the game's director. “No more hand-written code,” the director is said to have told the devs, with all art to be “generated with full AI workflows.”

Epic have, in general, bet big on generative AI. The tech is central to the next iteration of Unreal Engine, much to the displeasure of many game developers. Epic already use the stuff like a bike pump to inflate Fortnite character designs into something like a 3D model. They've also deployed it to voice-act Darth Vader, earning the ire of unions. Meanwhile, company CEO Tim Sweeney keeps complaining about Valve requiring genAI disclosures on Steam, evidently sensing an opportunity to lure AI-curious developers away to the perpetually ailing Epic Games Store.

The rush to make hay out of genAI comes as Epic's moneyhorse Fortnite starts to run out of kick. Epic laid off over 1000 people earlier in the year, with Sweeney citing a "downturn in Fortnite engagement". It's the company's largest layoff wave since Epic jettisoned 16% of their workforce in 2023, after spending too much money trying to turn Fortnite into a "metaverse" - that is, a new species of internet created by crossbreeding VR bodysuits with social media, the blockchain, and Ready Player One. The failure to make a metaverse of Fortnite doesn't inspire much confidence in Epic's current generative AI drive.

Disney took out a $1.5 billion stake in Epic this February. A couple of months later, Bloomberg reported that Epic had commissioned a Disney extraction shooter, alongside other Disney endeavours. It's not clear whether the extraction shooter is the same project referred to in the new article - the timeframes don't quite add up on paper, with Bloomberg's older article claiming that the extraction shooter was slated to launch in November.

The Fortnite publishers haven't confirmed or denied Bloomberg's account of events, but they have sent the outlet a statement in which they seek to qualify the "AI first" framing. "We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do,” writes Jake Jones, Epic communications director. Disney have yet to comment at all.

Bloomberg say that Epic staff have been joking about prompting the Claude software to fix its own errors. Others are hoping that Epic management will eventually have a change of heart, or weren't being serious in the first place. Assuming all of this is legit, I'd say there's some mileage to the latter hope, in that a lot of generative AI work isn't about actually working with the tools, but being seen to do so by a company's investors. In general, there's a familiar fake-it-till-you-make-it mindset at play among genAI's biggest advocates and backers; so much money has been sunk that everybody is under the cosh to keep up the charade.

body: Cristiano Ronaldo was visibly emotional ahead of Al Nassr’s AFC Champions League Elite match which had its kick-off delayed.
The start of the match against Uzbek champions Neftchi Fergana was pushed back 20 minutes due to a security alert.
Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Al Nassr won their delayed clash with Neftchi after appearing an emotional figure pre-match AFP
The clash on Monday at Alawwal Park had been scheduled to begin at 9.15pm local time in the Saudi Arabian kick-off.
However, the alert caused the match to be delayed until the necessary safety protocols and inspections had been carried out.
Supporters were permitted to remain in their seats whilst they waited for the action to get underway.
Ronaldo’s emotional gesture
Pre-match, Ronaldo was spotted kissing his shirt prior to the delayed kick-off against Neftchi.
The iconic forward kissed the swords and palm trees, representing the Saudi Arabian coat of arms, on his jersey.

He was also pictured holding the shirt up to his face to cover his eyes in an emotional moment, which seemingly saw him pay his respects to those who have lost their lives in recent missile attacks in the country.
Once the match was underway, the 41-year-old was on the scoresheet, as Ronaldo doubled Al Nassr’s lead before half-time after Angelo Gabriel had opened the scoring.
Neftchi would pull one back after the interval before a red card saw the visitors reduced to 10 men.
They would later score an own goal as Al Nassr ran out 3-1 winners.
And after the match, Ronaldo made sure to celebrate Saudi Arabia again, waving and wearing the nation’s flag on the pitch.

articles.headline: Trump Gets Brutally Fact-Checked For Claiming Denzel Washington Called Him A ‘Great Friend’
keyFacts: Donald Trump shared a social media post claiming actor Denzel Washington called him a great friend and steadfast supporter.
Fact-checking website Snopes reported that the quote is false and was previously attributed to Matthew McConaughey and Mick Jagger.
HuffPost reached out to representatives for Washington and the White House for comment.
body: President Donald Trump claimed that actor Denzel Washington was one of his most staunch supporters in a social media post on Monday … only to get publicly fact-checked.
Trump shared a social media post from the X account “Red Eagle Updates” that alleged that the Oscar winner had nothing but praise for the president, and even considered him a “great friend.”

“BOOM: Denzel Washington: ‘I’ve worked with a lot of people in my life, and I’ve never met anyone braver, smarter, or who cares more about America than Donald Trump. He’s a great friend and an even better president. I’m proud to be a steadfast supporter and I’ll never apologize for it,’” the original post read.
The post then asked social media users if they agreed with Washington’s so-called words.

The fact-checking website Snopes revealed that Trump’s repost is 100% false, noting that it had “found no reporting that Washington spoke favorably of Trump” on major news outlets like ABC News, CBS News, CNN, Fox News or others.

The website added, “If any actor of Washington’s prominence who had never publicly expressed such support in the past were to say the words attributed to them in the meme, national and international outlets covering entertainment and politics would have widely reported it.”
HuffPost has reached out to the White House and reps for Washington for comment.

The rumor-debunking site said that the same phony quote from Washington had also been previously attributed to actor Matthew McConaughey and Rolling Stones’ lead singer, Mick Jagger, in memes across social media.
Snopes also fact-checked erroneous reporting from 2018 that claimed that Washington said that electing Trump saved the U.S. from becoming an “Orwellian police state.”
Washington has generally abstained from aligning with political parties, and has criticized both the left and the right.
Speaking with the UK’s The Times in November 2024, Washington urged the public to realize they’re “being manipulated by both sides.”

Variety and other sources reported that the movie received middling reviews, including a 55 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes.
